legend.title: Risk judgement classes

irr.text:
Negligible for health
The occupational physician should still be consulted.

unc.text:
Uncertainty interval
Before classifying as negligible risk, double check the assigned scores, review the prevention and protection measures and consult the occupational physician for the final decision.

sup.text:
Above the negligible chemical risk
Apply Italian Legislative Decree 81/08 articles 225, 226, 229 and 230.

grave.text:
Severe risk
Reassess the prevention and protection measures and enhance surveillance, monitoring of chemical agents and maintenance frequency.

legend.defaultNote: P1 (Laboratory) and P2 (Rapid production) are pre-filled scenarios, not regulatory values: always verify quantity, duration, control, contact and distance against the actual task.
legend.defaultNote2: Quick preset → Controlled use, general ventilation, exposure < 15 min, quantity 1–10 kg, accidental contact level, distance 1–3 m (d = 0.75)
legend.normNote: Compliant with MoVaRisCh 2026 (28 February 2026) and Italian Legislative Decree 135/2024. Substances classified H340, H350/H350i, H360 and variants (categories 1A/1B) are NOT included in the MoVaRisCh P calculation and must be assessed separately under Title IX, Chapter II of Italian Legislative Decree 81/08.

tutorial.title: How to use the KEMIVAL parser
steps: Upload one or more safety data sheets (SDS) in PDF format from your device.
Click "Extract & Calculate" to extract the data and obtain a preliminary calculation.
Enter the reviewer once and confirm all SDS without blocking issues together; inspect only the flagged exceptions.
Verify that operating parameters and presets match the actual task, then review the risk judgement.
After confirmation, export Excel, Word or the cumulative report.

cmrWarning.title: ⚠ WARNING — CMR substance (category 1A/1B)
cmrWarning.body: The substance is classified as carcinogenic, mutagenic or toxic for reproduction in category 1A or 1B (detected H-statements: {codes}). Under Italian Legislative Decree 135/2024 (amending Title IX, Chapter II of Italian Legislative Decree 81/08, Article 234), these substances are NOT included in the MoVaRisCh hazard index P calculation and MUST be assessed separately as carcinogenic, mutagenic or reprotoxic agents. Apply Articles 235 and following: substitution, closed-cycle operation, health surveillance and the exposed-workers register.

normReference.title: Regulatory references
normReference.body: Calculation performed according to MoVaRisCh 2026 (Emilia-Romagna, Tuscany and Lombardy Regions — updated 28 February 2026) and Articles 222–232 of Italian Legislative Decree 81/08, as amended by Italian Legislative Decree 135/2024 (implementing EU Directive 2022/431). H-statement classification according to Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 (CLP) and the 22nd ATP (EU Regulation 2024/2564).

indexGuide.title: Guide to MoVaRisCh indices
indexGuide.intro: Meaning of the indices used in the health-risk calculation (Title IX, Chapter I of Italian Legislative Decree 81/08).

D.name: Physico-chemical properties
D.meaning: Physical state of the substance and its tendency to become airborne (liquid volatility or solid dustiness).
D.lab: Volatile organic solvent (acetone) used in small volumes → D=3 (medium/high-volatility liquid).

Q.name: Quantity in use
Q.meaning: Mass or volume of the substance handled per operation or work shift.
Q.lab: Weighing 50 mg of an analytical standard → Q=1 (< 0.1 kg).
Q.production: Transferring 25 kg of additive from a drum → Q=4 (10–100 kg).

U.name: Type of use (system)
U.meaning: Degree of process containment: closed, inclusion in a matrix, controlled or dispersive.
U.lab: Closed reactor with septum sampling → U=1 (closed system).

C.name: Type of control (ventilation)
C.meaning: Technical exposure controls: containment, local exhaust ventilation, general ventilation or direct handling.
C.lab: Operation performed in a fume hood → C=2 (local exhaust ventilation).
C.production: Work area with general room ventilation only → C=4 (general ventilation).

T.name: Exposure time
T.meaning: Cumulative duration of operator exposure during the working day.
T.lab: Sample weighing and preparation, 10 min → T=1 (< 15 minutes).
T.production: Continuous production line for 6 hours → T=4 (4–6 hours).

I.name: Exposure intensity index
I.meaning: Normalised exposure intensity, calculated as I = f(D × Q × U × C) using MoVaRisCh thresholds. A higher value indicates greater exposure intensity.
I.lab: Typical: low intensity (I ≤ 3) for analytical activities with effective containment.
I.production: Typical: medium-to-high intensity (I = 5–10) for uncontained production processes.

indexGuide.formula:
R_inal = P × E_inal = P × (I × d)
R_cut = P × E_cut
R_tot = √(R_inal² + R_cut²)
where P is the highest score assigned to the substance's H-statements (excluding CMR category 1A/1B).
